Hi Avery,

Thanks for the product overview last week. Before we move a production workload into Redwood, our security and privacy team needs a quick set of clarifications tied to the DPA transfer annex and the PII handling model. High level asks below — can you confirm and share a short dataflow diagram? If possible we'd like a 30–45 minute walkthrough.

Top asks:
- Short dataflow diagram showing where PII is tokenized/pseudonymized and where raw identifiers may be persisted (if any).
- Subprocessor roster with roles (processing vs support) and country of operation.
- KMS custody: where keys are held, whether keys leave customer VPC for hosted mode, and attestations for HSM/KMS access.
- Retention tiers for inference telemetry and whether telemetry is exportable under the transfer annex.
- Copy of the current DPA transfer annex draft or a pointer to the redline.

Can we schedule a slot this week or early next week for a short Q&A + walkthrough?

Thanks,

Head of Compliance, HealthSync

Hi Sofia — short technical clarifications ahead of the call so we can be focused: 

Snapshot answers (we'll expand on the call):
- KMS custody: For Hosted customers keys may be managed by customer-managed KMS (recommended) or Redwood-managed KMS. For the latter, keys are stored in our HSM-backed service; access to plaintext keys is restricted to the key management layer (no application-level export). We can provide an HSM attestation PDF if required.
- Subprocessors: our roster separates 'processing' subprocessors (inference GPU pools, storage for ephemeral caches) from 'support' subprocessors (monitoring, analytics). We'll mark columns in the CSV accordingly.
- Telemetry retention: default telemetry (token counts, latency, error rates) is aggregated for 90 days. Payload-level logs are configurable and off by default for privacy-first customers; if enabled they are retained per contract and gated under the transfer annex.

Items we'll bring to the walkthrough:
- A redline of the transfer annex with options for onshore-only routing or contractual carve-outs. (attachment: dpa_transfer_annex_draft.docx)
- A short checklist for exports and pseudonymization controls.

Requested inputs from HealthSync ahead of the call:
- Confirmation whether you need onshore-only subprocessor commitments or if contractual data routing + audit log access is acceptable.
- Example PII categories you consider 'sensitive' so we can highlight those paths in the diagram.

I'll be on the Wed/Thu slots above — Tue afternoon PST is tough.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dpa_transfer_annex_draft.docx]
